speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The merger was first announced in July last year and the merged entity will take on the name of ACRA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government's accountancy-related functions have evolved over the years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: ACRA was created in 2004, following the merger of the Registry of Companies and Businesses and the Public Accountants Board to consolidate complementary functions in financial statement regulation and audit regulation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: ACRA, currently, registers and regulates public accountants, business entities and corporate service providers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: ASC was formed in 2007 to set accounting standards that would apply to companies and non-corporate entities, such as charities, societies and co-operative societies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: SAC was set up in 2013 following a recommendation made by the Committee to Develop the Accountancy Sector (CDAS).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: SAC's key function is to grow the accountancy sector and related fields in Singapore, including the development of the Singapore Chartered Accountant Qualification (SCAQ), which leads to the conferment of the "Chartered Accountant of Singapore" designation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Government has reviewed the structure of these entities and assessed that there is value in consolidating these accounting-related functions within one entity.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The merger seeks to achieve the two key objectives while preserving the existing strengths of the constituent parts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One, it will strengthen the effectiveness of regulation, standard setting and sector development by harnessing synergies across complementary functions.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: ACRA has set up a sustainability reporting office and is taking the lead to monitor global reporting developments on this front.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: ACRA is also working with industry stakeholders to develop an implementation roadmap.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For the roadmap to be feasible, our accounting firms and professionals need to be equipped with the necessary knowledge.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Such capability building and sector development initiatives are, currently, overseen by SAC.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The merger of these entities will allow for closer partnership and forge a stronger feedback loop between regulatory and sector development matters, enabling us to respond more nimbly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We expect more of such cross-cutting issues in the future, for example, on the valuation of intangible assets and implications on financial reporting standards.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Thus, the merger of these entities is timely.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Two, it will strengthen the merged entity's ability to develop and manage talent in a sustained manner as well as provide better career development opportunities to officers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Today, SAC and ASC secretariats are both small organisations with a staff strength of less than 30 officers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: By merging them with ACRA, which has a wider range of responsibilities and larger staff strength of about 200 officers, there will be more opportunities for existing SAC and ASC secretariat officers to be cross-deployed, cross-trained and move forward in their careers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Bill seeks to give effect to the merger through two key sets of amendments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The first set of amendments relates to amendments to the ACRA Act and the repeal of the SAC Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Currently, the SAC Act provides for the SAC to perform the functions and powers relating to the growth and development of the accountancy sector and its related fields, such as business valuation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The SAC Act also provides for SAC to register persons as Chartered Accountants of Singapore and handle issues relating to the suspension or termination of such membership.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Bill also provides for SAC's assets, liabilities, records and employees to be transferred to ACRA with no change to the employment terms of SAC's employees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: SAC's current employment terms are the same as those of ACRA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Consequentially, the SAC Act will be repealed and the SAC dissolved accordingly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Savings and transitional provisions have been provided under Part 5 of the Bill to ensure that the handover from SAC to ACRA can be smoothly effected, for example, where there are pending applications relating to Chartered Accountants of Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The second set of amendments pertains to amendments to the Accounting Standards Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Currently, ASC sets accounting standards that apply to companies, charities, societies and co-operative societies in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Following the merger, the Bill provides for an Accounting Standards Committee to be established within ACRA.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The appointment of members to the Committee will have to be approved by the Minister for Finance, as is the case with the appointment of members to ASC today.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This would allow the Accounting Standards Committee, which will now be reconstituted under ACRA, to continue performing its function of setting accounting standards in the same way as the Accounting Standards Council does today.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Bill also provides that the accounting standards made or formulated by ASC that are currently in force will remain valid, until otherwise superseded by the Accounting Standards Committee.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Part 3 of the Bill provides for the amendments to the Accounting Standards Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These are to allow non-ACRA Board members to be appointed to the Public Accountants Oversight Committee, and to replace existing references to “Singapore Accountancy Commission” with “Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority” and existing references to the “Accounting Standards Council” with “Accounting Standards Committee”.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Accountancy has continued to thrive because of the key role it plays in supporting capital markets and businesses, and it continues to evolve and remain relevant to industry needs.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As reflected in the Accountancy Jobs Transformation Maps for In-house Finance and Accounting Functions and Accounting Practices, job roles in accountancy continue to evolve and new roles are emerging, in tandem with the rapidly changing business landscape.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I commend the Government for the Jobs Transformation Maps and various other initiatives to upskill and reskill the profession.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: All professions have to constantly adapt to changes arising from technological advancement and climate change, and the accountancy profession, in particular, is adapting well.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: These developments reflect the need for the Government to prepare accountants for emerging roles.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Therefore, the merger of the accountancy-related units in ACRA, SAC and ASC secretariats into a strengthened accountancy function under one entity is a step in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This merger will strengthen the effectiveness of regulation, standard-setting and sector development by harnessing synergies across complementary functions.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The merged entity will also be better able to support the needs of the accountancy profession as Singapore transitions to a green economy.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Looking ahead, there are pertinent areas that need to be enhanced to further grow the accountancy sector and profession.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For instance, there is a misperception that the accountancy sector is no longer an attractive career.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The Business Times reported that students are choosing courses that will lead to hot jobs in fields, such as data science and environmental sustainability, over accountancy.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This seems to contradict with my observations, as there is now a severe shortage of accountants in the jobs marketplace, with demand outstripping supply.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The talent shortage in the accountancy sector is an urgent issue and we need to develop the accountancy talent pipeline to meet the projected demand to support the growth of Singapore’s businesses and the economy.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: More needs to be done to increase the supply of professional accountants.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The first area is on the enhancements to the Singapore Chartered Accountant Qualification (SCAQ).

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: SCAQ is the gateway to the future of the accountancy sector.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is the main qualification pathway for one to qualify as a Chartered Accountant of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As the national Chartered Accountant (CA) qualification, SCAQ is an important product of Singapore and a brand with the potential to be marketed regionally and internationally, just like the renowned ACCA, which is a key export of the UK.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It should be reviewed and enhanced holistically to be more in line with market expectations.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Given the diverse roles professional accountants can play in an increasingly complex business environment, SCAQ should be designed to cater to a wider range of career pathways.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I note that SCAQ, currently, contains a module on valuation but does not delve deeper into the topics of sustainability and forensics.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For the existing valuation module, a review should be undertaken to consider if the curriculum should be broadened to provide appreciation of pertinent valuation issues driving the businesses currently, for example, changes and impact to businesses caused by climate change and/or other ESG factors.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The review can be conducted jointly with the Institute of Valuers and Appraisers Singapore, which is supported by the Singapore Accountancy Commission currently.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To further enhance the programme’s value proposition, it should focus on attracting a wider audience to inject talent diversity through the review of the programme entry requirements and structure enhancements, increasing flexibility on how practical experience is recognised and exploring regionalisation opportunities.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For greater inclusivity and to widen the talent pool beyond those who have pursued accountancy tertiary studies, having multiple entry pathways and recognition of relevant competencies would improve the profession’s accessibility.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The second area is the need to tighten policy and enhance regulation of preparers of financial statements.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: While we build the talent pool, it is important to also look at upholding financial reporting quality, which is crucial to maintaining Singapore’s reputation as a global financial centre and business hub.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Accountants in Singapore are, primarily, unregulated as long as they are not public accountants.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Under the Accountants Act, only those who provide public accountancy services must register with the Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There are no regulations governing those who provide non-audit services like accounting, taxation or consultancy, financial services and those who are employed in business, commerce and industry.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Furthermore, the title "accountant" is used loosely, as any individual can practise and declare themselves an accountant.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: There is no incentive for unregulated accountants to continuously upskill or adhere to ethical requirements as they are not required to comply with continuous professional development requirements and are not answerable for misconduct or any forms of discredit to the accountancy profession.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For instance, unregulated accountants who are not kept abreast of the anti-money laundering regulations and sanctions may be susceptible to being used by money launderers as they may not be aware of the latest money laundering methods and trends.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Another concern is the impact of poor quality financial reporting on audits and the effective functioning of capital markets.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Relevant and reliable financial information is core to the functioning and integrity of our capital markets and it supports the reputation of Singapore as an attractive place of business with strong financial systems and credible finance as well as accounting professionals and advisors.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Furthermore, unregulated accountants and accountancy services can lead to a negative perception of the accountancy profession and its competencies.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This will help ensure that the entire financial reporting value chain is subject to proper and adequate quality control.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The third area is the need to boost sustainability skillsets.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As I mentioned in my Parliamentary speech last month, the accountancy profession plays a critical role in supporting Singapore’s transition towards a green economy.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Accountants are required to meet the demands arising from these trends, which include decarbonisation, sustainability reporting and green finance.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: CFOs and finance managers will need to manage carbon trading.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They need to understand carbon markets, credits and measurement of emissions, as well as sustainability reporting frameworks, guidelines and principles.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They also need to navigate different and difficult regulatory and sustainability frameworks, both regionally and internationally.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Audit and assurance professionals will require upskilling in sustainability reporting and assurance requirements.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They will also be called upon to enhance internal processes.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Audit professionals and tax advisors, CFOs and finance teams must understand and apply carbon tax regulations and guidelines, both regionally and globally.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: With the sustainability movement being at a nascent stage, there is insufficient skilled talent in this area.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: More must be done to equip the accountancy profession with certifiable skills in sustainability.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In this regard, the Government can partner professional bodies, like ISCA, in preparing the accountancy profession for the transition to a green economy.

speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
text: To conclude, I commend the Government again on its efforts to ensure greater alignment among the Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: It was just a presumption that you would not be speaking.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: This Bill is an important step in that direction.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It will streamline the regulation of accountancy in Singapore and put ACRA in a stronger position to shape the development of the accountancy sector.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: My first point is on the process for revoking or suspending a Chartered Accountant’s (CA) registration.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The new section 35F provides the procedures for revoking or suspending a CA’s registration, which must be done in line with the designated entity’s rules.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Minister clarify whether designated entities will be required to provide in their rules a right for the CAs to be heard before any revocation or suspension?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Section 35G allows ACRA to review steps taken by a designated entity for any contravention by a CA where the entity did not take any action against the CA or, having taken such action, suspends the member’s registration or imposes any lesser penalty.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Minister clarify whether ACRA has the power to conduct a review in two further situations?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: First, where the entity took action and, ultimately, decided not to make any order against the CA.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Second, where the entity took action and decided to revoke the CA’s registration.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I ask these because section 35G(2)(b) on the situations where ACRA may conduct a review refers specifically to suspension but not revocation by an entity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: On conducting a review, section 35G(3) and (4) give ACRA the power to revoke registration, extend suspension, or suspend registration.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It appears that ACRA has the powers to impose heavier, but not lighter sanctions than those initially imposed by the designated entity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Minister clarify if ACRA has the powers, on a review, to impose lighter sanctions, or overrule the designated entity’s decision and not impose any sanction?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Under section 35G(5), before revoking, suspending or extending the suspension of a CA’s registration, ACRA must give the person written notice of its intention to do so and an opportunity to submit reasons against ACRA’s decision.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Minister share why the opportunity for the CA to submit reasons appears to come only after ACRA has come to an initial view on whether the CA’s registration should be revoked or suspended?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Will the CA be provided an opportunity to submit reasons before ACRA makes an initial determination at all?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: My second point is on ACRA’s powers to delete designated entities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Under section 35L, before deleting a designated entity, ACRA must give the entity written notice of its intention to do so and the opportunity to submit reasons.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Minister share why the opportunity to submit reasons comes only after ACRA has come to a view whether the entity should be deleted?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Will ACRA inform the designated entity that its designation is currently under review and provide the entity a chance to respond even before it takes a position on the deletion?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Minister share what considerations ACRA will take into account in deciding whether a designated entity should be deleted?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: This will provide guidance to entities in providing reasons why they should not be deleted.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: My third point is on retaining talent in accountancy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: In January this year, the Singapore Accountancy Commission (SAC) worked on and unveiled a new Job Transformation Map (JTM) for the accounting industry intended to chart a path forward for the sector in a post-COVID-19 world and introduce support initiatives to upskill and redesign jobs in this field.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: This is a welcome step forward for the industry, which is currently being transformed extensively by digitalisation and technology, and even newer drivers, such as climate change.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It will help safeguard jobs and create new ones.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: However, while JTM will address concerns on the supply side, more work can be done on the demand side.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: With ACRA's broadened scope to develop the accountancy sector and oversee qualifications and programmes relating to the sector with the dissolution of SAC, what measures will be explored as part of JTM, or otherwise, to attract and retain accountancy talent?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: My final point is on climate and sustainability-related accounting standards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Part 3 of the Bill introduces a new Accounting Standards Committee, which will take over the functions of the Accounting Standards Council (ASC).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: ASC is responsible for making and prescribing accounting standards for use by various entities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: ASC takes reference from the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB), while taking into account local business and economic needs and circumstances.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: IASB is currently working on a set of global, climate and sustainability-related disclosures designed to meet the information needs of investors in assessing enterprise value.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Has the Council, or will the Committee, evaluate its stance on these new green standards?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I was so hopeful there for a moment, but always happy to have Mr Louis Ng's speeches and to respond to them.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Members raised questions around three themes: one, the processes to revoke or suspend Chartered Accountants and delete designated entities (DEs); two, regulating those who prepare financial statements; and three, talent-related challenges and emerging trends in the accountancy sector.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Louis Ng sought a few clarifications on the process of revocation or suspension of a CA's registration and deletion of DEs from the Act.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: There are no changes to these provisions arising from the merger.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Today, ISCA is the only designated entity, appointed by SAC, to confer the Chartered Accountants' designation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I will now address Mr Louis Ng's questions, in turn.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: First, Mr Louis Ng asked whether DE's will be required to provide, in their membership rules, a right for CAs to be heard before they revoke or suspend a CA's registration.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is not provided for under the Act because the rules of natural justice would apply to accord affected CAs with the right to be heard before any adverse action can be taken against the CA.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Second, Mr Ng asked about two aspects of ACRA's powers with respect to DEs and CAs: one, whether ACRA has the power to conduct a review, if DE did not take any action against the CA in respect of an alleged contravention by a CA, or if DE has revoked the CA's registration; two, whether ACRA has the power to impose lighter sanctions than what DE meted out or to overrule the DE's decision upon review.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: ACRA's review power is limited to revocation, suspension or extending a suspension on a CA.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Such review power is intended to deal with cases where more punishment than what DE has meted out may be warranted.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: If such a CA is aggrieved by the decision of DE, including the DE's revocation or suspension, of his or her registration, and feels that his or her case is deserving of a lighter punishment, there is a separate channel for the CA to appeal to ACRA, under section 35 of the Act.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In an appeal, ACRA has the power to then take various actions as necessary, including quashing the revocation or suspension of the CA.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Third, Mr Louis Ng asked why the opportunity for the CA and DE to submit reasons arises only after ACRA has reached an initial view on whether the CA's registration should be revoked or suspended, or the DE's designation deleted respectively.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In practice, ACRA will review the relevant materials in the proceedings that the DE has previously undertaken, which will, typically, include the explanation given by the CA before arriving at the preliminary view of an intended revocation or suspension.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Member should rest assured that the final decision will only be made after allowing the CA an opportunity to be heard.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Lastly, Mr Louis Ng asked for the factors that ACRA will take into account in deciding whether a DE should be deleted from the Act.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When we appointed a DE, which is ISCA today, it is because we see a role for DE in ensuring professional competence, standards and ethics of CAs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As part of the appointment, the roles and responsibilities of DE are specified and agreed between DE and SA currently, or, in future, ACRA.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The arrangement enables the Government to work with partners to build and nurture a strong accountancy sector.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In assessing whether to continue with or delete a DE from the third schedule of the Act, ACRA would take into account the effectiveness of the arrangement with the DE, in ensuring that the desired outcomes for the sector are met, as well as the ability of the DE to fulfil the roles and responsibilities.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Next, I move on to Mr Don Wee's suggestion to regulate those who prepare financial statements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Specifically, Mr Don Wee suggested to mandate the chairpersons of Audit Committees of publicly-listed companies to be a CA and all financial statements of publicly-listed companies to be signed off by a preparer who is a CA.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Today, the code of corporate governance already requires at least two members, including the Chairperson of the Audit Committee, to have recent and relevant accounting or financial management expertise and/or experience.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This takes into account the need for the Audit Committee members to have diverse finance and accounting skillsets, and experience in business contexts beyond a professional designation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Under the Singapore exchange listing rules, listed companies must comply with the Code of Corporate Governance or provide justifications for non-compliance in the Annual Report.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Today, we hold directors responsible for the preparation of financial statements, given their fiduciary duties to shareholders over the company's finances.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Don Wee and Mr Louis Ng raised concerns on the talent shortage in the accountancy sector and highlighted the need to do more to expand the talent pool.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Ensuring a healthy pipeline of talent is, indeed, important.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This Committee comprises key industry players, including our national professional body for accountancy, the Institute of Chartered Accountants (ISCA) and academia.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will share more details about the recommendations in due time.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Don Wee asked for a review of SCAQ, in particular, areas, such as entry pathways and curriculum coverage, as well as to include emerging areas, such as forensics, valuation and sustainability, in the SCAQ curriculum.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The council and committees draw representatives from the industry and academia, some are also ISCA members.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I agree with Mr Don Wee that a more comprehensive and holistic review of SCAQ from time to time is useful.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: This is one of the areas that AWRC will look into.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: ISCA has also, separately, convened an SCAQ advisory panel to assess and provide recommendations to the Government on possible enhancements to SCAQ.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I look forward to the recommendations of the panel.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Next, I will touch on sustainability, a trend that both Mr Louis Ng and Mr Don Wee highlighted in their speeches.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Don Wee suggested that the Government partner professional bodies to help accountancy professionals build capabilities in sustainability-related areas, such as sustainability reporting and assurance requirements.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will continue to monitor these trends and see how the Government can do more to enable the green agenda.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Beyond building capabilities, there have been calls for more consistent sustainability reporting standards to facilitate comparison.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Mr Ng asked if the Accounting Standards Committee would be developing a position on the future sustainability-related standards set by the International Sustainability Standards Board, or ISSB.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Currently, ACRA and the Singapore Exchange RegCo have set up the Sustainability Reporting Advisory Committee, comprising relevant industry stakeholders, to develop a sustainability reporting implementation roadmap.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Part of the committee's work is to study various reporting standards, bearing in mind the need for international convergence.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Just like how things are evolving around the world, the Government will continue to respond with agility and transform ourselves to better serve the industry.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The merged entity will build on the good work done by ACRA, SAC and ASC and continue to work closely with industry players to grow the accountancy profession and sector.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: There being no clarifications, I will put the question.      .
